messages.content: You are a precise information extraction system. You only output valid JSON.

Find all event triggers of the event types below in the document.

Event types:
- Attack: An agent physically assaults or launches a violent attack on a target (bombing, ambush, raid, shooting, assault). (e.g. attack, assaulted, ambushed, bombing)
- Military_operation: Organised armed conflict between forces: a war, battle, campaign, siege or military operation as a whole. (e.g. war, battle, fought, campaign)
- Conquering: An agent takes control of a place or group by force (capture, seize, conquer, occupy). (e.g. captured, conquer, seized, taken)
- Killing: A killer causes the death of a victim (an agent is responsible for the death). (e.g. killed, killing, murdered, massacre)
- Death: Someone dies, with focus on the death itself rather than on a killer. (e.g. died, death, dead, deaths)
- Bodily_harm: Someone is physically injured or wounded. (e.g. injured, wounded, injuries, hurt)
- Catastrophe: A natural or man-made disaster happens (storm, flood, earthquake, crash, fire, accident). (e.g. hurricane, storm, flood, earthquake)
- Destroying: Something is destroyed completely (destroyed, demolished, sunk, burned down). (e.g. destroyed, destruction, demolished, sank)
- Damaging: Something is damaged but not completely destroyed. (e.g. damage, damaged, struck, battered)
- Statement: A speaker communicates a message (says, states, announces, describes, reports). (e.g. said, stated, announced, described)
- Change_of_leadership: Leadership or control of a polity or organisation changes (election, coup, revolution, ousting, independence, replacement of a leader). (e.g. elected, coup, revolution, ousted)
- Arriving: An agent arrives at or reaches a place. (e.g. arrived, reached, entered, landed)

Trigger annotation rules:
- A trigger is the single word (sometimes a short phrase) that most clearly expresses the event; it can be a verb ("attacked") or a noun ("attack", "war", "fires").
- Annotate EVERY occurrence: if the same event is mentioned several times ("the fires ... the fires ..."), list each occurrence as a separate entry.
- Only annotate the 12 event types below; ignore other kinds of events.
- Disambiguation:
  * Military_operation = a war, battle, campaign or siege as a whole; Attack = one specific assault, bombing, raid, shelling or ambush.
  * Conquering = capturing or taking control of a place or group (captured, seized, took, defeated and occupied).
  * Killing = someone or something kills (killed, massacre, slain, executed); Death = the dying itself (died, death, dead, fatalities).
  * Catastrophe = the disaster event itself (storm, hurricane, fire, flood, crash, accident); Destroying = something is completely destroyed; Damaging = something is damaged but not destroyed.
  * Bodily_harm = injury or wounding (injured, wounded, injuries).

Return JSON: {"triggers": [{"trigger": "<word copied from the document>", "type": "<event type>"}]}
List one entry per occurrence, in reading order. Return {"triggers": []} if there is none.

### Example 1
Document:
The June 2011 Christchurch earthquake was a shallow magnitude 6.0 earthquake that occurred on 13 June 2011 at 14:20 NZST (02:20 UTC). It was centred at a depth of, about 5 km (3 mi) south-east of Christchurch, which had previously been devastated by a magnitude 6.2 M earthquake in February 2011. The June quake was preceded by a magnitude 5.9 M tremor that struck the region at a slightly deeper 8.9 km (5.5 mi). The United States Geological Survey reported a magnitude of 6.0 M and a depth of 9 km (5.6 mi). The earthquake produced severe shaking, registering at VIII on the Mercalli scale in and around Christchurch. It destroyed several structures and caused additional damage to many others which had been affected by previous earthquakes. The damaged tower of the historic Lyttelton Timeball Station collapsed before dismantling work could be completed. The earthquake downed phone lines and cut off power to 54,000 households. Restoration costs in Christchurch following the February earthquake were estimated to increase by NZ $6 billion (US $4.8 billion) because of the additional damage from this event. Forty-six people suffered injuries, two of which critical, and one elderly man died after being knocked unconscious.

{"triggers": [{"trigger": "earthquake", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "devastated", "type": "Destroying"}, {"trigger": "earthquake", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "quake", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "struck", "type": "Attack"}, {"trigger": "destroyed", "type": "Destroying"}, {"trigger": "damage", "type": "Damaging"}, {"trigger": "damaged", "type": "Damaging"}, {"trigger": "dismantling", "type": "Destroying"}, {"trigger": "earthquake", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "damage", "type": "Damaging"}, {"trigger": "suffered", "type": "Bodily_harm"}, {"trigger": "died", "type": "Death"}]}

### Example 2

The 1985 Mexico City earthquake struck in the early morning of 19 September at 07:17:50 (CST) with a moment magnitude of 8.0 and a Mercalli intensity of IX (" Violent "). The event caused serious damage to the Greater Mexico City area and the deaths of at least 5,000 people. The sequence of events included a foreshock of magnitude 5.2 that occurred the prior May, the main shock on 19 September, and two large aftershocks. The first of these occurred on 20 September with a magnitude of 7.5 and the second occurred seven months later on 30 April 1986 with a magnitude of 7.0. They were located off the coast along the Middle America Trench, more than away, but the city suffered major damage due to its large magnitude and the ancient lake bed that Mexico City sits on. The event caused between three and four billion USD in damage as 412 buildings collapsed and another 3,124 were seriously damaged in the city.

On 22 July 2013, a series of earthquakes occurred in Dingxi, Gansu. The first quake struck at 07:45 China Standard Time with the epicenter located at the border of Min County and Zhang County. The magnitude of the initial earthquake was placed at M 6.6 by the China Earthquake Data Center with a focal depth of. It was measured at M 5.9 by the United States Geological Survey (USGS) and M 6.0 by the European Alert System. Another strong quake occurred about one hour later, measured at 5.6 magnitude by the USGS. As of 18:00 CST (10:00 UTC), 22 July 2013, 422 aftershocks had been recorded. The earthquakes were also felt in the nearby cities of Tianshui and Lanzhou in Gansu, as well as Xi'an, Baoji, and Xianyang in neighbouring Shaanxi. As of 23:00 CST, 23 July 2013, the earthquakes had caused at least 95 deaths, and more than 2,300 people had been injured.
